one_line: Agent-native live art auction discovery and bid preparation on Base.
what_it_does: Exposes auction, artwork, provenance, settlement, and bid-preparation actions so an agent can inspect live auction state while the human signs the transaction.
leverage_rationale: Structured auction state, provenance, eligibility, and bid preparation are materially more reliable than visual UI driving, though the human still signs the bid.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says the agent reads bids, deadline, and provenance through declared tools instead of guessing at pixels.
About text lists eleven tools including active-auction search, auction state, provenance, prepare_bid, and place_bid.
Frame sheet visibly shows a tool menu and a returned list of open auctions.
execution_rationale: The dark auction UI, artwork detail state, and visible tool-driven open-auction query form a coherent end-to-end slice; full transaction settlement is not shown.
execution_evidence: Video frames show the ArtSoul auction interface with artwork, auction panel, ETH values, and no-bids state.
Frames show agent query for open auctions and returned artwork/auction identifiers.
Public repository and live demo are reported in the packet.
impact_rationale: Collectors and artists have a concrete need for trustworthy auction state and provenance, and the product addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: About text describes Base auctions with deposits, settlement, and provenance.
Tools expose deadline, bidder, owner, and event history rather than only presentation data.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared structured agent state to a live art-auction protocol, while preserving human signing authority, is a fresh and well-developed interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent-native auction discovery and bid preparation are central to the pitch.
The workflow connects protocol lifecycle and provenance to agent-readable actions.
usability_note: Clear auction context and human-signed transaction boundary; crypto onboarding may still add friction.
standouts: Human remains the signer for consequential action.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible demonstrated workflow.

one_line: A shared 3D hardware studio where humans and agents build and simulate machines.
what_it_does: Imports and arranges sourced components, validates wiring, controls a 3D workspace, and runs deterministic physical simulations with evidence attached to values.
leverage_rationale: The agent and engineer share live structured project state, component evidence, topology, and simulation results; general UI driving would be markedly less reliable for this workflow.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes one live 3D studio shared by humans and WebMCP agents.
About text lists tools for project inspection, asset loading, assembly, validation, view control, simulation, and result comparison.
Frames show a 3D robot asset, product data panels, and tool/status panels.
execution_rationale: The visual product is coherent and ambitious, with a recognizable 3D hardware workflow and agent operations; the frame evidence does not fully prove all simulation paths.
execution_evidence: Frames show a multi-view orange-and-black robot in a 3D/product workspace.
Frames show code-like tool cards for public data/status and asset loading.
Packet reports live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Hardware designers and educators can benefit from evidence-backed component selection and early validation before physical builds.
impact_evidence: About text identifies incompatible motors, batteries, wiring, and scattered specifications as the target problem.
Product preserves evidence status and supports deterministic experiments.
creativity_rationale: The combination of evidence-backed sourcing, shared human-agent 3D assembly, and simulation is unusually ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Concept joins product-page research with simulation-ready machine construction.
Agent actions appear in the same workspace the engineer is viewing.
usability_note: Rich workflow appears useful but hardware modeling and evidence management imply a substantial learning curve.
red_flags: Full end-to-end simulation result is not clearly legible in the viewed sheet.
standouts: Evidence status attached to engineering values is a strong safety-oriented detail.
advance_reason: High leverage and ambition with credible product-motion evidence.

one_line: A browser-native React workspace for human-agent editing, preview, recovery, and export.
what_it_does: Keeps files, diagnostics, live preview, checkpoints, and export in one workspace while WebMCP applies validated multi-file changes through the same services as UI actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured file mutations, diagnostics, checkpoints, and explicit outcomes reduce ambiguity and make shared revision state reliable; ordinary UI driving would be materially more fragile.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on people and Codex building, previewing, recovering, and exporting together.
About text describes ten operations with validated multi-file changes and shared revision state.
Packet states UI and tools call the same workspace services.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is unusually coherent for a small React workspace and the video packet shows editor/workspace progression, though not every recovery/export path is visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a structured workspace with navigation, cards, fields, and execution/output areas.
About text names deterministic starters, Sandpack preview, IndexedDB, checkpoints, and ZIP export.
Live demo and public repository are reported.
impact_rationale: Developers collaborating with coding agents have a concrete need for visual context, safe mutations, diagnostics, and recovery.
impact_evidence: About text identifies ambiguity and slowness of clicking through file trees as the target problem.
Checkpoint and diagnostic features directly address safe agent editing.
creativity_rationale: Reversing the usual agent-centric IDE model so the application remains the human-visible collaboration surface is a fresh interaction choice.
creativity_evidence: Product explicitly explores the application offering a precise collaboration surface to the agent.
Atomic multi-file edit with one checkpoint and revision is a focused concept.
usability_note: Preview, diagnostics, and recovery are colocated, though a coding workspace remains technical.
red_flags: Tool invocation text is not clearly legible in the viewed frame sheet.
standouts: Strong safety/recovery framing for agent edits.
advance_reason: Clear central workflow and meaningful WebMCP delta.

one_line: A transparent civic microgrid sandbox for agent-explored energy scenarios.
what_it_does: Lets an agent run bounded deterministic solar-and-battery scenarios, compare trade-offs, diagnose outages, and shortlist a plan while a human sets criteria and approves the result.
leverage_rationale: Structured deterministic scenario tools and shared visible criteria make agent exploration auditable and repeatable, beyond generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says AI explores deterministic scenarios while humans retain final authority.
About text lists seven tools for baseline, scenario runs, comparison, diagnosis, and shortlisting.
Frames show outage proof, visible metrics, and human-owned criteria.
execution_rationale: The packet and frames show a coherent scenario-to-decision workflow with transparent metrics, outage handling, and an approval boundary.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show grid at 0 kW, eight of eight hours coverage, and planning metrics.
About text describes three scenarios, comparison, shortlist, approval, and print-ready brief.
Live demo and public repository are reported.
impact_rationale: Small councils and housing associations have a real early-stage resilience-planning need, and the product directly clarifies budget, emissions, and outage trade-offs.
impact_evidence: About text names climate/resilience officers and an indicative grant/feasibility decision.
Frames show budget, emissions, resilience, and outage outcomes together.
creativity_rationale: The combination of deterministic civic planning, visible trade-offs, and explicit human authority is a strong, thoughtful application of agent collaboration.
creativity_evidence: Human sets criteria and approves while agent explores the bounded decision space.
Outage proof and transparent decision brief are pursued as first-class interaction states.
usability_note: The staged scenario, metrics, and approval framing make a consequential technical choice legible.
red_flags: Agent tool calls are inferred from the product sequence rather than clearly legible call logs.
advance_reason: Best balance of demonstrated completion, impact, and auditable leverage in the packet.

one_line: An address-first Danish property and infrastructure information explorer.
what_it_does: Combines property, utility, environmental, and map-source information around an address and exposes structured retrieval and navigation tools to an agent.
leverage_rationale: Structured retrieval across fragmented public datasets is useful and reduces search friction, but a capable general agent could reproduce much of the lookup workflow with effort.
leverage_evidence: About text lists address verification, property, utility, environmental, map-layer, and source tools.
Frames show a consolidated address information card and a technical/agent panel.
Agent and person can inspect the same address profile.
execution_rationale: The address-first interface and consolidated information card are coherent, but the packet notes the application pre-existed unfinished and provides no gallery images; frame evidence is mostly presentation-oriented.
execution_evidence: Frames show a polished responsive property/infrastructure landing and example address card.
About text describes Next.js implementation and multiple public data sources.
Packet reports live demo and video but no gallery images.
impact_rationale: Homeowners, contractors, and advisers have a concrete need to find dispersed utility and property information before digging or renovating.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify fragmented registries, maps, municipal portals, and utility sources.
Hero visibly frames understanding an address before digging, buying, or renovating.
creativity_rationale: The address-first aggregation is useful and well framed, but the core property-information portal is a familiar category with a moderate agent-enabled twist.
creativity_evidence: Agent retrieves structured evidence while users follow original sources.
Language and Denmark-preserving navigation are thoughtful details.
usability_note: Address-first search and source links are understandable; public-data caveats may require follow-up.
red_flags: Packet explicitly says the application already existed before the challenge as unfinished.
No gallery images and limited legible tool-call evidence.
standouts: Clear consolidation of fragmented public information.
advance_reason: Credible impact and useful agent delta, despite thinner execution evidence.

one_line: A shared spatial canvas where humans shape image briefs and agents return generated assets.
what_it_does: Stores briefs, references, direction, results, and variations on a tldraw canvas while WebMCP reads and updates the live creative project and returns generated assets.
leverage_rationale: Durable spatial project state and exact recipe retrieval make iterative image work more inspectable and repeatable than a long chat prompt, though generation remains native to the agent.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes a shared visual workspace with Codex execution and canvas return.
About text lists recipe search, exact version retrieval, project revision inspection, context preparation, and asset return.
Frames show prompt, recipe/card, agent workspace, and generated visual states.
execution_rationale: The visual system appears polished and the core brief-to-result flow is coherent; exact generation completion is only partially visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show the ‘What would you like to make?’ creation UI, recipe cards, workspace panels, and visual previews.
About text defines a focused recipe-to-canvas workflow.
Packet reports nine gallery images, live demo, and public repository.
impact_rationale: Designers and creative teams have a real need to preserve references, constraints, and iterations rather than burying them in chat.
impact_evidence: About text directly identifies lost project state and handoff problems in conversational image workflows.
Canvas keeps brief, references, direction, results, and variations visible.
creativity_rationale: The spatial canvas as a durable shared brief for agent image generation is a fresh synthesis with meaningful interaction depth.
creativity_evidence: Curated recipes cover structured visual tasks including posters, brand exploration, and sequential storytelling.
Agent returns outputs to the correct canvas result area.
usability_note: Visual project state is easier to inspect than chat history, though recipe and canvas concepts add complexity.
red_flags: Generation is performed by Codex rather than a page-owned generator, limiting the product’s direct execution surface.
standouts: Strong durable-context model for creative collaboration.
advance_reason: Distinctive creative workflow with a meaningful shared-state delta.

one_line: A wedding seating planner where humans drag guests and agents enforce constraints.
what_it_does: Lets hosts arrange guests manually while agents add together/apart rules, propose and apply seating, and repair conflicts through the same live functions; tools register dynamically with plan state.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic capability registration, conflict-dependent tools, pending-proposal invalidation, and shared invoke logic make WebMCP part of the product’s state model, not a UI convenience.
leverage_evidence: About text says resolve_conflicts registers only while a conflict exists and unregisters when resolved.
Propose/apply seating separates drafting from human-visible commit and invalidates stale proposals after changes.
UI and agent calls route through the same invoke chokepoint.
execution_rationale: The small scope is exceptionally coherent, with explicit conflict, proposal, commit, and stale-state handling described and shown in the video packet.
execution_evidence: Frames show seating board, guest/table plan, and tool console with list_plan.
About text specifies identical UI/tool functions and state-dependent registration.
Vanilla implementation has zero runtime dependencies and a live demo.
impact_rationale: Wedding hosts have a specific, stressful constraint-satisfaction problem; the product directly reduces tedious manual rearrangement while keeping the host in control.
impact_evidence: About text gives realistic together/apart seating constraints.
Conflict repair and proposal approval map directly to the host’s task.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic tool surfaces that appear and disappear with domain state, plus stale-proposal invalidation, are unusually inventive and deeply pursued for a hackathon project.
creativity_evidence: Tool list itself changes live as the seating plan changes.
Pending apply_seating exists only while a proposal is pending and is discarded after intervening edits.
usability_note: Direct manipulation remains primary and agent assistance targets the hard constraint work.
standouts: Best evidence of state-aware WebMCP design.
Excellent human/agent parity and concurrency handling.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creative depth with a concrete, visibly demonstrated workflow.

one_line: A collaborative system-design interview studio with an agent as senior engineer.
what_it_does: Lets learners draw architectures, run traffic simulations, inspect SLOs and bottlenecks, and use agent tools to suggest and apply rewires before rerunning.
leverage_rationale: The agent can inspect the selected live diagram, modify it, run simulations, and return measurable feedback; generic chat or UI driving would add real friction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists get_architecture, get_selected_node, connect, run_simulation, and related live-canvas tools.
Pitch and description emphasize agent modifying the same canvas and rerunning the design.
Frames show a node-based workflow/canvas and configuration panels.
execution_rationale: The concept and editor are coherent, but the viewed frame sheet more clearly shows graph editing than a legible completed simulation result.
execution_evidence: Frames show connected workflow nodes, component palette, properties panel, and learning prompt.
About text defines use cases, traffic walk, overflow, p99, robustness, and iterative feedback.
Packet reports live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: System-design learners have a real need for repeated practice and expert-like feedback; measurable SLO feedback makes the loop credible.
impact_evidence: About text targets system-design interviews and whiteboard practice.
Simulation exposes p99, errors, robustness, and cost-oriented feedback.
creativity_rationale: Turning the agent into an interactive senior interviewer who edits and tests the learner’s diagram is a fresh educational interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The agent’s guidance appears as rewires and a second run rather than prose alone.
Use-case-specific naive starting graphs create a teaching loop.
usability_note: The visual editor supports learning, but system design and simulation concepts are inherently technical.
red_flags: Simulation outcome and agent tool calls are not fully legible in the viewed frame sheet.
advance_reason: High educational value and original interaction, with moderate evidence limits.

one_line: A policy sandbox for allocating scarce resources with simulation and approval audit trails.
what_it_does: Defines budgets and rules, receives agent requests, simulates allocation outcomes, compares policy versions, and routes decisions through human approval with an audit trail.
leverage_rationale: Agents can submit structured requests and inspect policy effects in a shared governed workspace, while approvals and audit state remain explicit; this is more than a generic form automation layer.
leverage_evidence: About text lists policy inspection, structured requests, simulations, comparisons, receipts, and audit trail.
Product framing centers on the same visible policy workspace for humans and agents.
Frames show policy, budget, approval, and explanation concepts across the product presentation.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the packet shows a broad, intentional policy workflow, but the viewed frame sheet is mostly slide-like explanatory packaging rather than live end-to-end execution.
execution_evidence: Frames show RuleRipple problem/product panels and policy concepts.
About text specifies shared budget, limits, governance, simulation, version comparison, and approval.
Live demo is reported, but no public repository is listed.
impact_rationale: Teams and agent-heavy projects have a real need to allocate scarce credits transparently and understand who gets resources and why.
impact_evidence: About text grounds the product in scarce AI-credit allocation among competing requests.
Audit trails, explanations, and approval controls address governance directly.
creativity_rationale: Policy simulation plus agent-governed resource allocation is a useful synthesis with clear ambition, though the underlying budgeting pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Policy version comparison and allocation explanations make rule changes inspectable.
Agent access is paired with human approval rather than autonomous spending.
usability_note: Governance surfaces are valuable but policy configuration may be complex for small teams.
red_flags: Frame sheet primarily shows explanatory/product slides, not clearly legible live tool invocation or result.
standouts: Clear audit and approval orientation for agent resource allocation.
advance_reason: Strong problem fit and governance concept, but execution evidence is thinner than peers.

one_line: An agent-assisted film production manager turning scripts into schedules, tasks, and call sheets.
what_it_does: Analyzes multilingual screenplays, extracts production breakdowns, builds weather-aware schedules, assigns department tasks, reports status, and exports call sheets through WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured screenplay breakdown, schedule generation, weather-aware rescheduling, and department status are high-friction multi-step operations where explicit tools improve repeatability and consistency.
leverage_evidence: Pitch names eight WebMCP tools for screenplay-to-production management.
About text lists analyze_script, get_weather_forecast, generate_schedule, assign_task, get_production_status, export_call_sheet, and scene controls.
The intended agent workflow coordinates ten-plus departments and weather changes.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is complete from script analysis through schedule, tasks, status, and call-sheet export; frame evidence shows a substantial production-management interface, though text is small.
execution_evidence: Frames show the ROYA product presentation and multiple production-management UI states.
About text specifies a full production pipeline and Arabic/English/French support.
Packet reports live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Film producers have a concrete coordination problem across departments and weather, and the proposed outputs directly reduce costly replanning and communication overhead.
impact_evidence: About text identifies spreadsheets, calls, paper call sheets, and weather-triggered replanning as the problem.
Outputs include schedule, department board, live status, and daily call sheet.
creativity_rationale: Weather-aware, multilingual, agent-operated production coordination is an ambitious and memorable application of WebMCP to a real professional workflow.
creativity_evidence: The product connects screenplay understanding to operational scheduling and call-sheet generation.
Moroccan production context and Arabic/English/French support deepen the concept.
usability_note: A single production view can reduce coordination burden, though production terminology and setup remain specialized.
red_flags: Exact tool-call text is not reliably legible in the available frame view.
standouts: End-to-end workflow reaches a concrete operational artifact: the call sheet.
advance_reason: High impact and coherent end-to-end scope with credible evidence.
